symptom: `mxcli sql --alias shop "delete from sales.orders"` deleted every row and printed "(0 rows)", which reads as an empty select; there was no read-only mode and no affected-row count.
file: sql/readonly.go ReadStatement / Run / executeReadOnly; cmd/mxcli/cmd_sql.go (--write). Test: sql/readonly_2362_test.go (needs MXCLI_TEST_PG_DSN)
cause: The CLI passed every statement to db.QueryContext; a DELETE returns no rows, so its effect looked like an empty result.
insight: **A keyword check is not a read-only mode.** `with d as (delete from t returning id) select * from d` starts with WITH and deletes on PostgreSQL; only the transaction stops it. Measured on PostgreSQL 16: with the read-only, rolled-back transaction the CTE fails and both rows stay; replacing it with a plain query (the revert) deletes them. Keep both layers: the keyword refusal gives the clear message, the transaction holds for what the keyword misses.
